about: Manual only (0%) and per-account thresholds 1-100%: the spec built for 1.5. Produced by workflow wf_4927df27-02c (3 designs, 2 judges, 1 synthesis), 2026-09-26. Decisions and rejected alternatives are also in docs/decisions/2026-09-24-remote-control-answers.md.
grafted: From engine: AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold:room:) returns an Optional that is nil for 0, a negative value or NaN. It is the one place that excludes an account, used by eligibleUtilization(trigger: .threshold), drainEligibleUtilization, rankedTargets' keepsFable and, through the same eligibleUtilization, AppState's fresh-reading check. That lets clarity's defaulted manualOnly closure and its re-check after the await both go.

From judge 2, wired differently: the exclusion lives inside 'the one rule'. The role logic stays in the pure engine and not in AppState. effectiveThreshold returns 0 for Manual only. plan() reads 0 on the ACTIVE account as 'leave at defaultThreshold, never drain', where defaultThreshold is a new REQUIRED parameter. A candidate at 0 gets no ceiling.

From engine: a loop test over every whole threshold T = 1...100 checking four things: 0 < ceiling < T; drain ceiling >= switch ceiling; both never go down as T rises; and the result matches the 1.4 formula for T 20-100 (switch) and T 2-100 (drain).
From engine: the drain room is min(1, T/2), not a flat 1, so at T = 1 the drain is never stricter than the threshold rule.
From engine: AccountOrder.fallback(from:) makes removeAccount fall back to the first account that is not Manual only, and to the first account only when every remaining one is Manual only.
From engine: 'Disable auto switch' is ambiguous (it could mean 'never switch away'), which is why the state is named for what it does.
From engine: pure CLIOutput.thresholdSet with an extra sentence when the account is the active one (it says you are on it and where you will be moved off).

From minimal: keep the existing "Default (%lld%%)" and "Switch at %lld%%" labels and keys. Add only the Manual only item and 10/20/30/40, and drop clarity's 'Use up to' rename and its AccountSwitchRule type. The tooltip calls AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling directly, so the words cannot drift from the rule.
From minimal: normalizedAccountThreshold rounds to a whole number, so a stored 0.4 can never show '0' while still being a target.
From minimal: write down what was left out on purpose (no flag, no alias, no remembered value, no confirmation), so a later session does not 'fix' it.
New: a unit test that the five app Localizable.strings tables share one key set (verified identical today, 252 keys each), plus a check that the new keys exist and the retired keys are gone.
rejected: A 'Disable auto switch' checkbox beside the menu: two controls for one decision, a possible contradictory state ('disabled' but 'Switch at 70%'), and the words could just as well mean 'never switch away from it'.

Engine design's saved 'picked by you' state (ManualPick in UserDefaults, a didSet on @Published activeAccount, pickedByUser passed through switchTo/performSwitch, AppControlling.isManualPick). The GUI never shows it, so one 'Manual only' label would mean two behaviours, and it is the largest AppState change. It does not fit one sitting.

Minimal design's '0 counts as reached at any reading': a deliberate manual switch to a Manual only account, or setting it on the account in use, would be undone about 5 minutes later, rewriting the live Claude login under running sessions.

Clarity's manualOnly closure in rankedTargets (defaulted to { _ in false }) plus an isManualOnly re-check after the verification await. That is a second test beside 'the one rule', and any caller that leaves the closure out silently lets Manual only accounts back in. The Optional ceiling replaces both.

Judge 2's literal wiring, where AppState.effectiveSwitchThreshold returns the default for the active Manual only account and 0 otherwise. The engine could then not tell the active account is Manual only, so the drain guard would need yet another input, and the role rule would sit outside the pure, tested engine.
Clarity's 'Use up to' rename, the column rename and the AccountSwitchRule type: label churn in five languages with no change in behaviour.
Remembering the previous custom threshold when Manual only is chosen: a hidden value that would come back into force later. Turning an account back on is one click on Default or a number.
CLI aliases 'off', 'never' and 'disable': 'threshold off' reads just as well as 'never switch away'. Only 'manual' and 0 are accepted.
Letting the global Default threshold go below 50: a 0% default would make every account Manual only.
A confirmation dialog when switching to a Manual only account by hand: the switch is deliberate and the labels already say what the account is.
A flat drain room of T - 1 (minimal): at T = 1 the drain would need exactly 0.0% while the threshold rule accepts 0.5%, which inverts their relationship.
A Stepper range of 0...100 (minimal): stepping down from 1% would silently turn an account off.

A 'Manual only' badge beside the name in the popover (engine): AccountSwitcherView.swift:109-119 and UsageDashboardView.swift:353-356 record the address truncating there. A separate quiet line and the card footer are used instead.

No protocol bump (minimal): correct only without a new AccountInfo field. manualOnly, with effectiveThreshold meaning 'where it is left', is clearer for an AI reading list_accounts, and the bump turns an old running app into 'Quit and reopen'.

Moving you off the account in use the moment you set it to Manual only: a settings change should not pull a live login out from under running sessions. The row caption and the CLI say what will happen instead.
Menu items below 10% (5%, 1%): the Stepper already reaches 1-9, and the menu already grows from 13 to 19 rows.
Showing the popover 'Manual only' label while auto-switch is off: with auto-switch off every account is effectively manual, so a label on one account would mislead.

spec.name: Manual only (0%) at the bottom of the threshold menu
spec.oneLine: Each account's threshold menu now goes below 50% (10, 20, 30, 40, and every whole number down to 1% with the stepper) and ends in one named choice, "Manual only (0%)". Auto-switch never moves you to that account, you can still switch to it yourself, and while you are on it auto-switch moves you off only at the default threshold.
spec.controlDesign:
Settings -> Accounts keeps one row per account, in priority order and draggable as today: [≡] [name, Active badge, email, "Weekly resets …"] … [threshold Menu] [Stepper].

There is no checkbox and no new window. 0 is the named last stop of the same menu, so there is one control, one stored value and no contradictory state such as "disabled but 70%". It is called "Manual only", not "Disable auto switch", because "disable auto switch" could equally mean "never switch away from it".

COLLAPSED MENU LABEL
It reads AutoSwitchSettings.normalizedAccountThreshold(account.switchThreshold):
- nil: "Default (90%)". Existing key "Default (%lld%%)"; the number follows the global default live.
- 1-100: "Switch at 40%". Existing key "Switch at %lld%%".
- 0: "Manual only" (new).
The Menu keeps .fixedSize(), so the name column truncates first.

MENU ITEMS, top to bottom
1. "Default (90%)": appState.setSwitchThreshold(nil, for:), unchanged.
2. Divider.
3. "Manual only (0%)": setSwitchThreshold(0). Built as Button("Manual only (\(Int(AutoSwitchSettings.manualOnlyThreshold))%)"), so its key is "Manual only (%lld%%)" and the % goes through the same formatted path as "Switch at %lld%%".
4. Divider.
5. "10%", "20%", "30%", "40%", then the existing "50%", "55%" … "100%", all Text(verbatim:) as today. thresholdChoices = [10, 20, 30, 40] + Array(stride(from: 50.0, through: 100.0, by: 5.0)). That is 19 rows, ascending like today, so the scale reads 0, 10, 20 … 100.

STEPPER
- Shown only when the normalized own value is 1-100; hidden for Default and for Manual only.
- Range: new AutoSwitchSettings.accountStepperRange (1...100), step 1.
- Same binding as today: get appState.effectiveSwitchThreshold(for:), set setSwitchThreshold.
- It reaches every whole number from 1 to 100. Stepping down stops at "Switch at 1%", so an account can never slide into Manual only by accident.
- Manual only is set only by its named item, or by 0/manual from the CLI and MCP.

TOOLTIP (.help on the Menu, computed per row)
It replaces the old key "When this account's usage reaches this level, auto-switch moves you to another account."
- Default or 1-100, with t = the value the account is left at: "Auto-switch moves you off this account at 90%, and moves you to it only while it is at 80% or less."
  - The second number is AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold: t, room: AutoSwitchEngine.hysteresis)!, the same function the engine ranks and verifies with, so the words cannot drift from the rule.
  - Both numbers are formatted as (v / 100).formatted(.percent.precision(.fractionLength(0...1))), which follows the user's locale: 10% gives "5%", 5% gives "2.5%".
- Manual only: "Auto-switch never moves you to this account. You can still switch to it yourself; while you're on it, auto-switch moves you off it at the default threshold (90%)."

ACTIVE-ROW CAPTION
When auto-switch is on AND the row is the active account AND it is Manual only, one more caption line appears under "Weekly resets …" (same .caption, .secondary): "You're using it now. Auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it."

UNDER THE LIST
- Orange caption (.foregroundStyle(.orange)): "Every account except the one you're using is Manual only, so auto-switch has nowhere to move you." Shown when auto-switch is on, an account is active, there are 2 or more accounts, and every account other than the active one is Manual only.
- The footnote is replaced by: "Drag an account to change the order. \"My order\" in Settings → General tries accounts from the top down, and every account list follows this order. A threshold other than the default applies to that account only. Manual only accounts are never switched to automatically; you can still switch to them yourself."
- SettingsAccountsTab gains @AppStorage(AutoSwitchSettings.enabledKey) private var autoSwitchEnabled = false, the same default SettingsView uses.
- Displayed default numbers come from AutoSwitchSettings.defaultThreshold (a stored 0 reads 90; values are clamped to 50-100). The existing @AppStorage threshold property stays, so the row redraws when the slider moves.

SETTINGS -> GENERAL -> AUTO-SWITCH
The Default threshold slider stays 50-100. Only two texts change (see newStrings): the caption under the slider and the explanation paragraph.

HOW EACH VALUE IS SET
- 1-100: pick the nearest menu item, then use the Stepper.
- 0: the "Manual only (0%)" item.
- Back to the default: the top item.
- Turning an account back on means choosing Default or any number from the same menu.
spec.otherSurfaces:
One word family everywhere: "Manual only" in the GUI, "manual" or "manual only" in the CLI, manualOnly in JSON.

POPOVER -> ACCOUNTS TAB (AccountSwitcherView.accountRow)
When auto-switch is on and the account is Manual only, a third quiet line appears under the plan/provider line:
- Label("Manual only", systemImage: "hand.raised"), .font(.caption2), .foregroundStyle(.textSecondary), .lineLimit(1)
- .help("Auto-switch never moves you to this account. You can still switch to it here.")
It is a new line, never a badge beside the name: the comments at AccountSwitcherView.swift:109-119 record the address wrapping mid-word on the 360pt panel. The Switch button is unchanged, with no confirmation.

POPOVER -> USAGE TAB CARD (UsageDashboardView.cardFooter)
A new last branch on the right of the footer shows the same Label and help. It appears only when the card is not switching and not showing the hover hint, auto-switch is on, and the account is Manual only.
- "Switching…" and "Double-click to switch" keep priority.
- Double-click works as before.
- The header is untouched; UsageDashboardView.swift:353-356 explains why nothing goes beside the address.

WHEN THE LABELS SHOW
Both popover labels need auto-switch to be on (@AppStorage(AutoSwitchSettings.enabledKey) in each view). With auto-switch off every account is effectively manual, so a label on one account would mislead. The Settings menu label always shows the stored value.

UNCHANGED
- Header, menu bar strip and widget: they show the active account's usage, not auto-switch policy, and the widget target compiles neither Account.swift nor the engine.
- `pixelswitch status`.

SETTINGS -> GENERAL
The two reworded texts above. The slider and the early-switch help text are unchanged.

CLI
- `pixelswitch accounts` shows "90% (manual only)" in the "Switches at" column, plus a legend line.
- The threshold and switch confirmations say "manual only" in words (see remoteControl).

MCP
list_accounts carries manualOnly, and three tool descriptions change (see remoteControl).

README.md
Lines 73, 131 and 134 are updated (see engineChanges).
spec.zeroSemantics:
HOW 0 IS STORED AND READ
- Stored as switchThreshold == 0.
- AutoSwitchSettings.effectiveThreshold keeps its body (normalized own ?? default), so it now returns the rule value 0 for a Manual only account.
- The pure engine is the only place that interprets 0, and it does so in two roles.

AS A TARGET: NEVER
- AutoSwitchEngine.ceiling(threshold:room:) returns nil for a threshold <= 0 (and for NaN).
- Every eligibility path goes through it:
  - eligibleUtilization(trigger: .threshold), on .windows and on .fable;
  - drainEligibleUtilization (.drainEarly);
  - rankedTargets' keepsFable.
- So a Manual only account is excluded under the threshold rule and early drain, on session/weekly and Fable, and under mostRoom, myOrder (skipped in place; the next account down is tried) and resetsSoonest.
- It is dropped before isSwitchable, so no Keychain read is made for it.
- AppState checks the chosen target with the same eligibleUtilization(trigger:), using a threshold read fresh by id after the await (AppState.swift:1118). An account set to Manual only while it is being checked therefore gets no ceiling, fails with "trying next", and cannot be landed on. No extra check or re-check code is needed.
- It is also never the removeAccount fallback, unless every remaining account is Manual only (AccountOrder.fallback).

AS THE ACTIVE ACCOUNT
- plan() computes activeRule = threshold(active). When that is 0, the trigger becomes AutoSwitchSettings.clampedThreshold(defaultThreshold).
- defaultThreshold is a new required plan parameter; AppState passes AutoSwitchSettings.defaultThreshold (50-100).
- The session/weekly trigger, then the Fable trigger when "Also switch when Fable runs out" is on, then fires exactly as for a Default account.
- Candidates are ranked by the usual strategy, with the usual 10-point room.
- If nothing is eligible, it stays, under the existing rule that "reached with nowhere to go still counts as reached".
- Once left, it is never returned to automatically.

EARLY DRAIN WHILE A MANUAL ONLY ACCOUNT IS ACTIVE: NEVER
plan()'s drain guard adds !activeIsManualOnly. You are only on such an account because you, or a sign-in outside PixelSwitch, put you there. Under Resets soonest, the drain would undo that choice after every 5-minute cooldown.

WITH AUTO-SWITCH OFF
0 only changes labels.

UNCHANGED
The 300 s cooldown after any switch, the 10-point room for other accounts, the one-fresh-reading verification budget, and the 50-100 global default.
spec.lowThresholdSemantics:
RANGE
Per-account values are whole numbers, 0-100. 0 is Manual only; 1-100 are thresholds.

ACTIVE SIDE (unchanged)
Auto-switch moves you off an account when its usage on a watched limit reaches T (activeUtil >= T).

TARGET SIDE
The rule is ceiling(T, room) = T - min(room, T/2).
- Threshold rule (room = AutoSwitchEngine.hysteresis = 10):
  - T 20-100: T - 10 exactly, unchanged. Every saved 50-100 account and the 50-100 default behave bit for bit as in 1.4.
  - T 1-19: T/2.
  - Examples: 100 -> 90, 50 -> 40, 20 -> 10, 19 -> 9.5, 15 -> 7.5, 10 -> 5, 5 -> 2.5, 1 -> 0.5 (only a nearly untouched account qualifies).
- Early drain (room = drainMinimumRoom = 1):
  - T 2-100: T - 1, unchanged.
  - T = 1: 0.5.

WHY NOT KEEP A FLAT T - 10
It puts the ceiling at or below 0 for T <= 10. "Switch at 5%" would then be a hidden second Manual only as a target while still pushing you off at 5%, and T = 10 would only accept exactly 0.0%. With this rule, only the explicit 0 excludes an account.

PROPERTIES, PINNED BY A LOOP TEST OVER T = 1...100
- 0 < ceiling < T. An account chosen at or under its ceiling cannot trigger on arrival, and the account just left cannot be a target again until its window resets, so there is no ping-pong at any value. Example: an account left at 6% is a target again only at 3% or less.
- The drain ceiling is always >= the threshold-rule ceiling.
- Both never go down as T goes up.

OTHER EFFECTS
- keepsFable (Most room left's Fable preference) uses the same ceiling.
- "Most room" stays own T - usage. Example: a 10% account at 2% has 8 points of room and ranks below a 90% account at 70%, which has 20.
- Switching frequency at very low values is still bounded by the unchanged 300 s cooldown.

EXACT ELIGIBILITY RULE (one function, shared by ranking and verification)
A candidate is eligible for a threshold switch on `limit` iff all of these hold:
1. c = ceiling(T_candidate, 10) is not nil.
2. usage(limit) <= c.
3. For a Fable switch, session/weekly <= c as well.
4. isSwitchable(candidate).
For an early drain, c = ceiling(T_candidate, 1), plus the existing reset-timing conditions and the existing Fable check.
spec.manualSwitchRule:
SWITCHING TO A MANUAL ONLY ACCOUNT BY HAND
- It works like any other switch: the popover Switch button, a Usage-card double-click, `pixelswitch switch <account>`, or MCP switch_account.
- There is no confirmation.
- performSwitch is unchanged and restarts the 300 s cooldown, as every switch does (AppState.swift:798-801).

AFTER THE COOLDOWN
Auto-switch treats the active Manual only account as if it had the default threshold (for example 90%):
- It moves you off only when its 5-hour/weekly usage, or its Fable usage when that is watched, reaches the default.
- Early drain never moves you off it.
- Once you have left it, by hand or automatically, auto-switch never brings you back.

NO HIDDEN STATE
The same rule applies however the account became active:
- you set Manual only on the account you are on;
- a sign-in or re-authentication;
- Claude Code was signed in outside PixelSwitch;
- a launch with it active.

SETTING MANUAL ONLY ON THE ACCOUNT YOU ARE USING
This never, on its own, moves you off it. Two places say so:
- the Settings row caption: "You're using it now. Auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it."
- the CLI confirmation adds: "You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it."
To leave it straight away, switch by hand.
spec.storageAndMigration:
STORAGE
- The same field and key as today: Account.switchThreshold: Double? in the saved accounts JSON in UserDefaults.
  - nil = follow the default (unchanged; an account on the default still writes no switchThreshold key);
  - 0 = Manual only;
  - 1-100 = its own threshold.
- There is no new field, no separate flag and no new UserDefaults key.

NORMALIZATION
- AutoSwitchSettings.normalizedAccountThreshold now rounds to a whole number and clamps to 0...100. A rounded value <= 0 becomes 0, so there is never a -0.
- Before, it clamped to 50...100.
- Every value saved today is already whole: menu steps of 5, stepper steps of 1, and the API already rounds. So no saved account changes.
- isManualOnly(own:) is normalized == 0.

RANGES
- thresholdRange (50...100) is kept, for the GLOBAL default only: the Slider, SettingsCatalog autoSwitch.threshold and clampedThreshold.
- New: accountThresholdRange (0...100) and accountStepperRange (1...100).

MIGRATION: NONE
- 1.4's setter clamped to 50, so saved values are nil or 50-100. They decode and behave exactly as before.
- Their ceilings are unchanged for T >= 20 (switch) and T >= 2 (drain), and the active-side trigger is unchanged. Tests pin this.
- A saved global default of 0 still reads 90, so the default can never become Manual only.

TURNING AN ACCOUNT BACK ON
- Choose "Default (90%)" or any number from the same menu, `pixelswitch accounts threshold <account> default|<n>`, or accounts.setThreshold with null or a number.
- Nothing is remembered: choosing Manual only overwrites a custom value such as 70.
- This is deliberate. A remembered value is hidden state that would come back into force later; what the menu shows is the whole state. Record it as a decision so a later session does not add memory without a reason.

DOWNGRADE TO 1.4
- 1.4 reads a stored 0, or any value from 1 to 49, as 50 in the engine. Its row label prints the raw value ("Switch at 0%", "Switch at 35%"). The value stays on disk.
- "Update automatically" is on by default since 1.4, so a downgrade needs a hand-installed old DMG. The 1.5 release notes should say that Manual only and thresholds below 50% need 1.5 or later.
spec.remoteControl:
ControlProtocol.swift
- `version` goes from 1 to 2. AccountInfo gains a required field, which the file's own rule covers ("bumped whenever a method, parameter or result changes shape"). An old app still running after an update then gets the existing "Quit and reopen PixelSwitch" from CLIRunner.checkProtocol, instead of a decode failure or a confusing "must be 50–100".
- ThresholdParams.threshold doc: "1–100; 0 = manual only (auto-switch never switches to it); nil follows the default threshold."
- AccountInfo docs:
  - `threshold`: "own threshold: 1–100, or 0 for manual only; nil when it follows the default".
  - `effectiveThreshold`: "where auto-switch moves off this account while it is active: its own threshold, else the default (also when manualOnly)".
  - NEW `let manualOnly: Bool`, after effectiveThreshold: "true when auto-switch never switches to it; a person or accounts.switch still can".

ControlAPI.swift
- accounts.setThreshold: `guard value.isFinite, AutoSwitchSettings.accountThresholdRange.contains(value.rounded()) else { throw ControlError(.invalidValue, "A threshold must be 1–100, 0 for manual only, or null to follow the default.") }`, then `threshold = value.rounded()`.
  - 0.4 becomes 0 (manual only); 0.6 becomes 1; 35 is accepted; -1 and 101 are refused.
  - null still means follow the default.
- makeInfo: `effectiveThreshold: AutoSwitchSettings.leaveAtThreshold(rule: controller.effectiveSwitchThreshold(for: account), defaultThreshold: controller.autoSwitch.defaultThreshold)`.
- ControlSnapshots.accountInfo (signature unchanged) sets `manualOnly: AutoSwitchSettings.isManualOnly(own: account.switchThreshold)`.
- AppControlling, AppController and the tests' FakeApp are unchanged.
- settings.get/set autoSwitch.threshold is unchanged: still 50–100, through thresholdRange.

CLIParser.swift
- Syntax: `pixelswitch accounts threshold <account> <1-100|default|manual>`.
  - "default" gives .threshold(a, nil).
  - "manual", in any case, gives .threshold(a, 0). Use the literal 0: the CLI target compiles only PixelSwitchCLI/ and ControlProtocol.swift, never AutoSwitchEngine.swift.
  - Anything else is parsed as a number with a trailing % stripped, as today, so "0" and "0%" also give 0. The app validates the range.
  - "off", "never" and "disable" are deliberately not aliases and fall through to the parse error.
- Usage error: "Usage: pixelswitch accounts threshold <account> <1-100|default|manual>"
- Parse error: "The threshold must be a number from 1 to 100, \"default\", or \"manual\" (0 means manual too)."
- Help: the line becomes `pixelswitch accounts threshold <account> <1-100|default|manual>`, followed by a continuation line at the description column (like the sign-in line): "manual (or 0): never switched to automatically".
- CLICommand.threshold doc: "nil: back to the default; 0: manual only".

CLIRunner.swift / CLIOutput (pure, unit-tested)
- NEW CLIOutput.switchesAt(_ a: AccountInfo) -> String: percent(a.effectiveThreshold), plus " (manual only)" when a.manualOnly, else " (default)" when a.threshold is nil. It gives "90% (default)", "70%" or "90% (manual only)". CLIOutput.accounts uses it; the header stays "Switches at".
- CLIOutput.accounts: when any account is manualOnly, one more legend line follows the existing one: "manual only: auto-switch never moves you to it; switch to it yourself with pixelswitch switch <account>". With none, the output is unchanged (still 4 lines for two accounts).
- NEW CLIOutput.thresholdSet(_ a: AccountInfo?) -> String, replacing the inline closure in the .threshold case:
  - nil: "Threshold set."
  - threshold nil: "<email> now follows the default threshold (90%)." (unchanged)
  - manualOnly: "<email> is now manual only: auto-switch never switches to it. You can still switch to it yourself." When isActive, it adds " You're using it now: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it."
  - otherwise: "<email> now switches at 70%." (unchanged)
- NEW CLIOutput.switched(_ a: AccountInfo?) -> String, used by .switchAccount: "Switched to <name>." When manualOnly, it adds " It is manual only: auto-switch moves you off it at 90% and won't move you back to it."
- --json simply carries manualOnly.

MCPServer.swift (the tool count stays 18; the instructions text is unchanged)
- set_account_threshold:
  - Schema: "minimum": 0 (was 50), "maximum": 100, type number|null.
  - Description: "Set the usage percentage (1–100) at which auto-switch moves off this account; another account is switched to only while it is at least 10 points under its own threshold (at or under half of it, below 20). 0 makes it manual only: auto-switch never switches to it; a person or switch_account still can, and while it is active auto-switch moves off it at the default threshold. Null or omitted: follow the default threshold. 100 uses the account until it is empty."
- list_accounts: "Every account in priority order, with its usage, its switch threshold (manualOnly true: auto-switch never switches to it; effectiveThreshold is where auto-switch moves off it while it is active), and whether it can be switched to."
- switch_account: "Make this account the one Claude Code uses on that Mac. Returns when the switch is done. Works for a manual-only account too; auto-switch then moves off it only at the default threshold."
- get_settings and set_setting are unchanged.
tests: AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: a per-account threshold runs 0–100 while the default stays 50–100': accountThresholdRange == 0...100, accountStepperRange == 1...100, thresholdRange == 50...100, manualOnlyThreshold == 0. The existing 'thresholds run 50–100 and the drain window 1–72 hours' check still passes.

AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: a per-account threshold is stored as a whole number within 0–100': normalizedAccountThreshold of -5 is 0, 0 is 0, 0.4 is 0, 0.6 is 1, 35 is 35, 72.6 is 73 and 120 is 100; nil and .nan give nil. The existing 120/70/nil/nan check is kept.
AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: 0 is Manual only and nothing else is': isManualOnly(own:) is true for 0 and 0.4, and false for nil, 1, 50 and 100.

AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: an account's own threshold below 50 is kept, Manual only's rule value is 0, and the default still clamps to 50': effectiveThreshold(own: 35, default: 90) == 35; (own: 0, default: 90) == 0; (own: nil, default: 30) == 50 (existing).
AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: a Manual only account is left at the default': leaveAtThreshold(rule: 0, default: 90) == 90; (0, 70) == 70; (0, 30) == 50; (35, 90) == 35; (90, 70) == 90.

AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: a Manual only account saves switchThreshold 0 and loads it back': a JSON round trip gives 0 and isManualOnly true. The existing 'an account on the default saves no switchThreshold key' check stays.

AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: accounts saved by 1.4 behave exactly as before': decoded JSON with switchThreshold 50, 75, 100 or absent gives effectiveThreshold 50, 75, 100 and 90, and none is Manual only.
AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: a saved default of 0 still reads 90, never Manual only': UserDefaults autoSwitchThreshold = 0.0 gives defaultThreshold == 90 (inside the existing save/restore block).
AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: the hysteresis is 10 points': AutoSwitchEngine.hysteresis == 10.

AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: ceiling: 10 points under from 20% up, half the threshold below': ceiling(100,10) == 90, (50,10) == 40, (20,10) == 10, (19,10) == 9.5, (10,10) == 5, (5,10) == 2.5, (1,10) == 0.5.
AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: ceiling: the drain's 1 point, or half the threshold below 2%': ceiling(90,1) == 89, (2,1) == 1, (1,1) == 0.5.
AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: ceiling: Manual only has none': ceiling(0,10), (0,1), (-5,10) and (.nan,10) are all nil.

AutoSwitchRulesTests / 'rules: ceiling: every whole threshold 1–100 leaves room, never reaches it, and the drain's is never tighter': loop T = 1...100 with c = ceiling(T,10)! and d = ceiling(T,1)!: 0 < c < T, c <= d < T, and c and d never go down as T rises.

risks: The active side jumps between "Switch at 1%" and "Manual only (0%)". 1% pushes you off almost at once after the cooldown, while Manual only lets you stay until the default. The "(0%)" in the item could also read as "switch at 0%". Handled with different words, a per-row tooltip that spells out both numbers, and a Stepper that stops at 1 so one can never slide into the other.

Setting Manual only on the account you are using does not move you off it, and he might expect it to. This is deliberate: a settings change should not pull a live login out from under running sessions. The row caption and the CLI confirmation say exactly when he will be moved; switching by hand leaves at once. Record it as a decision.

If every other account is Manual only, auto-switch has nowhere to go and he runs the active account to its limit. The orange line in Settings → Accounts shows this, and the existing "no candidate verified; staying put" log is unchanged.

effectiveThreshold now returns 0 for Manual only. A future caller that treats it as 'where the active account is left' would bring back the rejected behaviour of leaving at any reading. Mitigation: plan's defaultThreshold is REQUIRED, so the engine's one active-side reading of 0 cannot be skipped; every display and the control API go through leaveAtThreshold; and the 'manual only, active' tests pin it.

The harness hides a CLI compile error. It compiles AutoSwitchEngine.swift together with the CLI files, so CLI code that uses AutoSwitchSettings passes the unit tests but breaks the real pixelswitch target, which compiles only PixelSwitchCLI/ and ControlProtocol.swift. The CLI uses the literal 0, and scripts/typecheck.sh (which type-checks the CLI target on its own) must be run before committing.

Choosing Manual only forgets a custom value such as 70%. Turning the account back on means picking it again, or one click on Default. Recorded as a decision (no hidden memory) so a later session does not 'fix' it silently.

Downgrading to 1.4 by hand reads 0 and 1–49 as 50. The account becomes a target again under 40%, while its row shows the raw 'Switch at 0%' or 'Switch at 35%'. The release notes should say this needs 1.5 or later; auto-update on by default makes a downgrade unlikely.

Very low limits can look like Manual only. A 5% account whose weekly use is already above 2.5% (for example from another Mac) is never a target until it resets. The tooltip states the exact 'at 2.5% or less', so this is explained, not hidden.

Protocol bump to 2: right after an update, an old app still running makes the new pixelswitch say 'Quit and reopen PixelSwitch' once. That is the check working. The existing status test uses ControlProtocol.version, so it passes.

The new target rule below 20% could in theory change existing behaviour. It cannot: every saved value is nil or 50–100. The loop test proves the result is identical to 1.4 for 20–100 (switch) and 2–100 (drain), and the whole existing rules suite must pass with only the helpers edited.

Race: an account is set to Manual only while auto-switch is fetching its verification reading. It is covered with no extra code, because verification reads the threshold fresh by id after the await and ceiling(0) is nil. This is exercised by the verification test.
Rounding: an API value such as 0.4 becomes Manual only, and 0.6 becomes 1%. No saved value changes, because every GUI path and the API already produced whole numbers.
The popover labels hide while auto-switch is off, so he may look for them there. The Settings → Accounts menu always shows 'Manual only'.

Early drain never moves him off an active Manual only account, even under Resets soonest with early switching on. The Manual only tooltip says he is moved off 'at the default threshold', and the early-switch help text is deliberately not reworded, to keep string churn down.

Localization: German and French texts are longer. The menu keeps .fixedSize() and the name column truncates first. The new l10n parity test fails if any of the ten keys is missing from a language, or a retired key is left behind.
The Default slider stays 50–100 and he may expect it to go lower. The General caption now says per-account limits go down to 1% or Manual only; a 0 default would starve every account.
The threshold menu grows from 13 to 19 rows, which is acceptable for a macOS pop-up. The Stepper covers every whole number from 1 to 100.

removeAccount now skips Manual only accounts when choosing a fallback. Behaviour changes only when the top remaining account is Manual only, and the first account is still used when every remaining one is Manual only.
